You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Use this when a task supplies several visually rich examples but none obviously matches the test input.

- Classify each demo by input structure and transformation family, not only by output appearance. Examples may show diagonal seeds expanded into circulant tilings, horizontal sequence continuation, or completion of a small missing cell; these are not interchangeable just because outputs are periodic or colorful.
- Record the test's structural signature (e.g. full-width colored bars separated by blank rows) and check whether any demonstration contains a comparable signature. Count of examples is not evidence of coverage.
- Spend further demo requests on a case likely to share the test geometry or distinguish candidate rules under it. State which uncertainty that request targets.
- If the demo cap approaches without structural coverage, do not invent a period, phase, palette, or operation from unrelated examples. Prefer a conservative inference only when a rule genuinely transfers across observed cases; otherwise recognize uncertainty rather than disguising a guess as evidence.

Case note: task-88ba74f4's test consisted of four full-width color bars (3, 7, 9, 1) separated by 0. Its seven demos showed other families, including diagonal/circulant tilings, row-sequence continuation, and small missing-cell completion. Those examples did not establish the test transformation; a diagonal-periodic submission was unsupported. This case illustrates why structural matching matters, not a solution rule for future tasks.", "file_type": ".md", "_source_path": "/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-hermesagentlearner-1790682188/attempts/bb618762f26744bd8f9c54499677d1fe/system/state/hermes/skills/arc/continual-arc-rule-induction/references/structural-demo-coverage.md"}
